Concrete Repair & Resurfacing · Kissimmee, FL

Concrete Repair and Resurfacing in Kissimmee

A concrete repair or resurfacing job in Kissimmee costs $3–$10 per sq ft (resurfacing), a Florida market range as of October 2026. The city's population climbed from 79,229 in the 2020 census to about 85,591 by mid-2025, so brand-new driveways now sit next to originals from the early 1990s, and the two age very differently once cracking shows up.

A driveway from Kissimmee's median construction year has had three decades to move

Kissimmee's median year of home construction is 1992 (Census Reporter, Kissimmee), which puts a sizable share of the city's original flatwork past the point where hairline cracking, a widened joint or a dulled finish is ordinary wear rather than a warning sign. Whether a given job needs a full permit depends on whether it stays inside the existing footprint or expands it; call Permitting at 407-518-2379 to confirm before assuming a resurfacing job is exempt.

Osceola isn't on the state's sinkhole-claims list the way some nearby counties are

A 2010 Florida Senate interim report names eleven counties that together accounted for more than 88 percent of sinkhole insurance claims filed statewide between 2006 and 2009: Hernando, Pasco, Hillsborough, Pinellas, Marion, Polk, Orange, Alachua, Citrus, Miami-Dade and Broward (Florida Senate Interim Report 2011-104). Osceola isn't one of them. A dip or crack in a Kissimmee driveway is far more likely to trace back to loose fill under the original pour, a cracked irrigation line, or ground that simply holds water close to the surface for part of the year than to the abrupt collapse the state's catastrophic ground-cover-collapse coverage is written around.

Why a cut-out panel needs its own base, not a patch on the old one

Replacing a single damaged panel means rebuilding the base under just that section, compacted to the same standard as the rest of the driveway rather than left loose because it's a smaller job. A new panel poured over soft, uncompacted fill settles again within a season or two, which defeats the point of cutting it out in the first place. On a Kissimmee lot, that base work usually means removing whatever caused the original failure, often a wet spot that never drained, before any forms go back in. The base under one panel gets the same attention the base under a whole driveway would.

A mudjacking day: holes, grout, and watching the slab rise

Once the void is confirmed, the crew drills a grid of small holes through the slab, typically 1 to 2 inches across, spaced to reach the full area that's settled. Grout gets pumped into each hole under pressure while someone watches the slab's edge with a level, stopping the moment the panel reaches grade rather than overshooting it. Each hole gets patched with a matching mortar once the lift is done. On a Kissimmee job, the holes are the only visible trace of the work once the patches cure, small circles across an otherwise unchanged driveway surface.

Resurfacing an original Kissimmee driveway, worked out in square feet

Say a 390 square foot two-car driveway, original to a house built around the city's 1992 median, is showing a network of hairline cracks and a chalky, worn surface. Resurfacing it at $3–$10 per sq ft (resurfacing) works out to somewhere between $1,170 and $3,900, cheaper toward the broom-finish end and pricier if a decorative overlay gets added at the same time. A full tear-out and repour instead would shift the job into driveway pricing territory and whatever permit process, city or county, actually covers that address.

The grout mix behind mudjacking, and the foam behind polyjacking

Mudjacking works through small holes, usually about 1 to 2 inches across, drilled in a grid pattern, then a soil-cement-water slurry is pumped under pressure until the slab lifts back to grade. Polyjacking uses smaller holes, closer to 5/8 inch, and injects a two-part polyurethane foam that expands within the void in minutes rather than filling it with liquid grout. Mudjacking nationally runs about $4 to $9 per square foot, polyjacking about $8 to $25, a gap that largely reflects material cost rather than labor. Either method leaves a small patched hole pattern across the Kissimmee driveway once the job is done.

Grout that's heavier than the ground can carry

Mudjacking's slurry has real weight, and on soil that's already weak or saturated, usually flatwoods ground with a shallow water table, that added weight can be too much for the base to hold, so the newly lifted slab settles again within a year or two. Polyjacking's lightweight foam is often the better fit on that kind of ground precisely because it doesn't add the same load. A Kissimmee contractor skipping a soil check before choosing between the two methods risks solving the dip today and creating the same call again next rainy season.

Caring for a fresh overlay without undoing the bond

A resurfaced driveway depends on the overlay staying bonded to the old slab underneath it, and an aggressive pressure wash too soon after the job, especially with a narrow tip held close to the surface, can chip or peel a thin overlay before it's fully cured. Sealing it on a schedule and avoiding harsh degreasers in the first few months protects that bond while it's still establishing. For a Kissimmee homeowner, treating a new overlay gently for its first season is a small habit that extends how long the resurfacing actually holds up.

Frequently asked questions

Should I worry about cracking in an original 1990s Kissimmee driveway?

Not automatically. With the city's median home dating to 1992, hairline cracking and worn joints on a driveway that age are typically routine wear, not a structural issue. A sudden, deep depression rather than a gradual crack is the kind of thing worth a closer look.

Does Osceola County see the sinkhole activity that Orange County does?

No, it isn't on the Florida Senate's 2010 list of eleven counties with the heaviest sinkhole insurance claims from 2006 to 2009, unlike neighboring Orange County. Settlement from loose fill or a wet subgrade remains the more common explanation locally.

Is a permit needed to resurface an existing driveway in Kissimmee?

A full replacement goes through the same review as a new driveway, but work that stays inside the existing footprint is usually a lighter submission. Confirm the scope with Permitting before assuming a resurfacing job is exempt.
